father_hypothesis.subject: Glasgow-3678
father_hypothesis.basis: Joseph Glasgow-1543 is selected as a possible biological father of William Glasgow-3678 at 30% subjective confidence. The published 1831 will names a William Glasgow who was raised by Joseph and leaves remaining property to that William’s children. The local William/Sally household, William’s circa 1788 birth and Joseph’s birth before 1765 permit fatherhood; the unnamed 1810 Wythe male 16–25 is compatible. The newly read 1829 original confirms this married William locally but names no parent. This is an explicit working inference from a specific caregiving and testamentary family context, not a literal parent statement.
father_hypothesis.limitations: Two propositions remain unresolved: which William the will means, and whether upbringing denotes biological sonship. William Glasgow-563, born 1778, Robert-12’s son, married 1802 with children born 1803–1822, is a substantive compatible alternative will subject; Ohio residence from 1805 does not exclude earlier upbringing or a legacy. William P. Glasgow-559, born 1813, has a later known family and is a weaker comparison, not categorically excluded. The will names no wife or residence for William. It explicitly calls Arthur’s son Robert a nephew and gives him the real-estate balance and furniture; William’s children receive the remaining property, not the whole estate. A nephew or another related dependent remains a strong alternative to biological sonship. The 1810 young man is unnamed. No mother, vital date, original tree or live WikiTree attachment is changed. Joseph’s own James-1024 father remains 35%; William’s four existing child grades remain 45/54/57/89%. This 30% combines identity and biological-role uncertainty; no multiplication or measured frequency is claimed.

source_readings.deed: Original image 183 of DGS 008562846 was downloaded through the authorized viewer and read 24 October 2026. William Glasgow and Sally his wife convey 190 acres on Reed Creek, a branch of New River, Wythe County, to Stephen Sayers for $1,050. Boundaries name Isaac Brown and John Craig. Both Glasgow spouses sign/seal. James Graham and Jacob Haller certify 14 December 1829; both acknowledgments describe the deed as 8 June 1829. The opening day is faint; the earlier biography’s 3 June 1829 is retained as a date discrepancy rather than silently harmonized. Recorded 12 January 1830. The complete entry contains no named Glasgow kin, inherited-title recital or acquisition history.
source_readings.will: Full published transcription rechecked 24 October 2026; no original image on the cited page.
source_readings.death_abstract: Clarita H. Morgan, Births and deaths 1853–1871, on record in Pulaski County Courthouse: actual PDF p. 135, death-index p. 9 (Freeborn G section), and PDF pp. 160–161, copied death-register pp. 14–15, were visually checked. No personal William Glasgow death was located there. This is a bounded negative in a published copy, not inspection of the original county register or proof that no death entry exists. The 1859 same-surname enslaver entry on PDF p. 154, copied register p. 8, row 7, is another person’s death, not William’s death or evidence naming his parents. The reported 1865 death remains unverified; no death field is changed.

prior_canonical_will.source_title: Joseph Glasgow will, Wythe Will Book 4, pp.1–3; published transcription rechecked 17 October 2026

prior_canonical_will.note: Joseph names his deceased brother Arthur and Arthur’s son Robert, the testator’s nephew. This corroborates brotherhood and distinguishes the younger Robert. It does not name Joseph’s father.
